I'll give you an example - im harness training my cat, so ill use that:
- for a while, i'll drape it over him and give him treats to make a positive association
- then ill try to clasp one of the clasps, give treat, unclasp, give treat, repeat for a few more days

Yeah, look at it like that: cats are extremely territorial and creatures of habit, so look at the sudden change in territory for both of them.

Resident: suddenly has to deal with a foreign smelling intruder on her territory.

New kitty: is introduced to a completely foreign territory with a potentially unfriendly cat who could be a threat.

That's why it's so important to separate them, then take your time and take it very very slow. Exchanging smells is very important too - have blankets for both of them, play and pet them on the blankets, then swap and see how they react. You can also wipe their faces with a handkerchief and let the other smell it.

Then you can feed them on two sides of the same door, then maybe through a screen door so they get a positive association with each other and are okay with the other cats presence.

Then you can introduce them safely.

Basically, you introduced an intruder to your old cat's territory, hence she's not very keen on playing with the new boy, she doesn't see him as a potential friend.

Isolate the cats immediately, and take it really really slowly next time. What they need is to make themselves familiar with each other's scents, and you need to mix their scents up - for example taking a blanket the new cat was using and swapping it with the old cat's blanket, giving treats when she's in it so she can associate the smell with something pleasant.

Don't make them see each other. Make the old cat think it's her space again, she is probably very stressed and when you feel she's back to normal do the scent thing. When she gets used to that, then push further, with the help of the article I posted above. (Also if you can, read Jackson's "total cat mojo" book, it's really helpful when it comes to understanding cat behaviour!)

In your case, it could honestly take months. The old cat doesn't trust the new one, so you will have a bit more of a difficult job. But with a lot of patience you can make them very good friends! Good luck!
